name: Bodyweight Split Squat
tierNote: Safety tier C (content.md appendix B: not in A or B lists; bodyweight only); census.json difficulty tier 1.

claims.text: From a split stance, bend both knees to lower until the back knee lightly touches the floor.

quotes.text: Bend both knees to move down until the back knee lightly contacts the floor.

claims.text: Keep the trunk upright; a very slight natural shift toward the front leg is fine, but the front shin stays about vertical at the bottom.

quotes.text: Keep the trunk upright and allow yourself to shift very slightly toward the front leg naturally, but keep the front shin approximately vertical in the bottom.

claims.text: Come up until the front knee is about straight.

quotes.text: Reverse the motion until the front knee is approximately straight.

claims.text: Split length changes the emphasis: front foot farther forward works the back of the hip and thigh more and stretches the rear hip flexors; closer works the quads more.

quotes.text: The farther forward the front foot, the more the exercise will rely on the posterior chain and stretch the rear hip flexors; the farther back the front foot, the more the exercise will rely on the quads.

claims.text: The split squat helps balance a weaker leg or hip and builds glute strength and hip stability.

quotes.text: help balance weakness in one leg or hip, build better glute strength and hip stability

claims.text: Sets of 5-10 reps at a load that allows smooth movement with no crash into the bottom (Catalyst gives this for the loaded split squat).

quotes.text: Sets of 5-10 reps are usually appropriate with weight that allows a smooth movement and no crashing into the bottom position.

claims.text: In a loaded study, lunging up and down with the feet fixed (a split squat) produced less glute activity than stepping out and back.

quotes.text: lunging up and down with feet stationary
gluteus maximus and gluteus medius EMG activities were significantly greater in lunges with a stride compared to lunges without a stride.

claims.text: The split squat can be loaded with any implement: barbell, dumbbells, kettlebells or a sandbag.

quotes.text: The split squat can be loaded with any implement, from a barbell, to single or double dumbbells or kettlebells held in any position, to a sandbag.

claims.text: NHS knee-pain advice: get urgent advice (111) if the knee is very painful, or locks or gives way.

quotes.text: your knee locks, gives way or painfully clicks – painless clicking is normal

sources.title: Effects of Step Length and Stride Variation During Forward Lunges on Lower-Extremity Muscle Activity

plate.viewWhy: Static split stance in the sagittal plane; back-knee depth (c1), upright trunk and vertical front shin (c2) read from the side.
plate.start: Standing in a split stance, front knee about straight (c3), trunk upright (c2).
plate.end: Both knees bent, back knee lightly touching the floor (c1), front shin about vertical, trunk upright (c2).

checkpoints.label: Front shin vertical
checkpoints.what: Front shin about vertical at the bottom.

checkpoints.label: Back knee down
checkpoints.what: Back knee lowers until it lightly touches the floor.

mistake.what: Front knee slides forward at the bottom, front shin tips well past vertical.
mistake.why: The anchor allows only a very slight shift toward the front leg and keeps the front shin about vertical (c2).
mistake.rankNote: No source ranks split-squat faults by frequency; this is the one position the anchor limits explicitly. The wrong pose is the inverse of c2.

tells.text: Back knee lightly touches the floor

tempo.text: Smooth, no crash into the bottom. No source gives seconds.

setup.step: Stand in a split stance, one foot forward, one back.
Bend both knees until the back knee lightly touches the floor.
Keep the trunk upright and the front shin about vertical.
Stand back up until the front knee is about straight.

posture.point: Front shin about vertical at the bottom.
Front foot farther forward for more hip work, closer for more quads.

handlingMistakes.mistake: Front knee sliding forward at the bottom.
handlingMistakes.fix: Keep the front shin about vertical at the bottom.
Lower smoothly until the back knee just touches.

rows.means: A stretch in the rear hip flexors; expected, stronger with a longer split.

rows.where: Knee pain that is very bad, or the knee locks or gives way

risks.risk: Crashing into the bottom instead of lowering smoothly.

zooms.wrong: Front knee slid forward, shin tipped far forward.

zooms.wrongNote: The wrong drawing is the inverse of c2; no source describes it directly.

libraryDiff.why: Library: quads primary, glutes secondary. Catalyst (c4, c5) names quads and glutes; loaded EMG shows less glute activity with the feet fixed than when stepping (c7), which fits glutes as secondary. No change.

loadProgression.text: Sets of 5-10 reps at a load that allows a smooth movement with no crash into the bottom; it can be loaded with dumbbells or other implements.

anchorNote: Catalyst Athletics Split Squat page read in full. It describes a barbell setup for weightlifters and says the split squat can be loaded with any implement (c8); it does not describe the unloaded version, so its stance, depth, trunk and shin cues (c1-c4) are applied to bodyweight on the reasoning that they do not depend on the load.
decisionNote: Stand-alone full card (fixer, 2026-09-30). The batch brief named reverse_lunge as the template parent, but reverse_lunge's hand archetype is hold (census) and this card's is none; content.md 2.3 requires a child to share its parent's hand archetype, and content.md appendix A lists bodyweight_split_squat as a stand-alone parent. Plate view (viewWhy) and the knee red-flag box (c9) are cited in this card, so nothing depended on the parent.
unsourced: A bodyweight-specific split-squat technique page (none found on ACE).
Rep range for bodyweight only (Catalyst gives 5-10 for the loaded version).
